conflicts.fact: Kepler's Third Law data/verification and Lesson 4's Solar System scale values
conflicts.versions: Lesson 4 gives Neptune 30.05 AU and 0.5 AU per square, so Neptune is about 60 squares, which is consistent. Lesson 4's model-building note says 'all inner planets fit within 1.52 AU' while the Observe phase says the four inner planets fit within 3 squares (1.5 AU). Both are consistent, so there is no real conflict.

conflicts.fact: Number of lessons the unit anchors and the lesson count referenced
conflicts.versions: Lesson 1 says the DQB anchors 'the remaining 11 lessons'; Lesson 12 teacher text says 'the past eleven lessons'. Both are consistent with a 12-lesson unit, so there is no real conflict.

conflicts.fact: What the Milky Way is and how many stars it has / galaxy count
conflicts.versions: Lesson 2 says the Milky Way is a barred spiral galaxy with over 200 billion stars. Lesson 12 says it is 'one of hundreds of billions of galaxies', which is a different quantity and does not conflict.

conflicts.fact: Evidence for the expansion of the universe from Hubble
conflicts.versions: Lesson 8 says Hubble deep field images show 'evidence for accelerating expansion' and also 'confirming cosmic expansion', while Lesson 12 attributes expansion to Hubble's redshift observations. This is slightly inconsistent in wording but not a hard contradiction.

conflicts.fact: Lake Victoria tides / tidal anomaly claims
conflicts.versions: Lesson 6 says Lake Victoria has detectable micro-tides and Mombasa has twice-daily tides. Lesson 9 claims the May 2024 storm caused a 'measurable tidal anomaly in Mombasa' and 'unusually high tides', attributing tides to a geomagnetic storm, whereas Lesson 6 attributes tides to Moon and Sun gravity.

conflicts.fact: Whether the cause of orbital laws was explained
conflicts.versions: Lesson 5 says the constant T²/r³ shows a single force 'yet to be fully explained' and describes planets farther from the Sun taking longer. Lesson 6 states Kepler's Laws were proved and gravity is the why. Consistent.

conflicts.fact: Age of Solar System / Milky Way formation
conflicts.versions: Lesson 2 says the Milky Way formed ~13.6 billion years ago and the Solar System ~4.6 billion years ago. Lesson 5 says the Solar System formed 4.6 billion years ago from the same nebula that produced the Sun; Lesson 4 says the Solar System formed from the same cloud left after the Big Bang. Consistent.

conflicts.fact: Kenya's satellite and the featured CubeSat
conflicts.versions: Lesson 8 says Kenya launched its first satellite (1KUNS-PF) from the ISS in 2018. Lesson 10 features the Kenya Space Agency's 'BIRD-5 CubeSat team' as satellite engineering, which is a different satellite name and does not directly conflict.

conflicts.fact: SKA described as largest radio telescope vs MeerKAT/SKA location
conflicts.versions: Lesson 7 says MeerKAT and the SKA project are in South Africa. Lesson 8 says Africa hosts the SKA, 'the world's largest radio telescope', which is consistent.
Lesson 8 says over 65 years of instrument-based evidence from 1957, consistent with Sputnik in 1957 and 2024 or later.

Lesson 9 says the storm was May 10, 2024, but the predict scenario describes radio silence on May 11 and the CME takes 17 hours to arrive while radio blackout from EM radiation is immediate (8 minutes); the scenario date is a day after the event, which is a small timing inconsistency.
